RT01.name: Data model, schema and identity design
RT01.scope: Run use-case workshops, map the client's entities into profile, event and lookup schemas, and choose the identity namespaces and primary identities the profile will merge on.
RT01.evidence: it is important to follow best practices for data modeling when designing your schemas

RT02.name: Data sources and ingestion setup
RT02.scope: Connect the agreed sources such as CRM, loyalty, commerce and web or app events, map fields to XDM, enable datasets for Profile and check that the first loads build the expected profiles.
RT02.evidence: You can ingest data from a variety of sources such as Adobe applications, cloud-based storages, databases, and many others.

RT03.name: Profile and merge policy configuration
RT03.scope: Set the merge method and dataset priority in the default merge policy, review how the identity graph links records, and check sample profiles against source data.
RT03.evidence: merge policies are the rules that Experience Platform uses to determine how data will be prioritized

RT04.name: Audience build and destination activation
RT04.scope: Build the starting audiences, connect the agreed destinations, choose the identities and attributes to send, then schedule and test the first activations.
RT04.evidence: After you configure your destination, you can activate audiences in multiple ways

RT05.name: Governance, access and sandbox setup
RT05.scope: Set up roles, permissions and development and production sandboxes, apply data usage labels and policies to datasets, and confirm activations respect those policies.
RT05.evidence: assist your team with the right permissions, access controls, and sandbox configurations

RT06.name: Monthly audience and dataflow operations
RT06.src: Adobe Experience Platform end-to-end example workflow
RT06.scope: Each month, review source and destination dataflows and alerts, fix failed runs, retire or refresh audiences, and add destinations as new use cases come in.
RT06.evidence: Experience Platform allows you to track how data is being processed through the use of dataflows

JO01.name: Access, sandbox and channel setup
JO01.scope: Set up roles and sandboxes, delegate the sending subdomains, and create the email and other channel configurations, IP pools and suppression and allowed lists.
JO01.evidence: Define all the technical parameters required for email, mobile messages, push notifications, web push, direct mail, and other channels

JO02.name: Journey events, data sources and actions
JO02.scope: Configure the identity namespaces, profile-enabled schemas and datasets the journeys need, then the journey events, data sources, custom actions and test profiles.
JO02.evidence: to be able to send messages in journeys, you must configure Data Sources, Events and Actions

JO04.name: Content templates and personalization
JO04.scope: Build reusable email and message templates and fragments, set up personalization and dynamic content, and preview rendering with test profiles.
JO04.evidence: Create reusable content templates and fragments to maintain brand consistency.

JO05.name: First journeys and campaigns
JO05.scope: Design, build, test and publish the starting journeys and campaigns, such as a welcome series, an abandoned cart journey and a scheduled campaign, with entry, wait and exit rules.
JO05.evidence: Build multi-step customer journeys to initiate a sequence of interactions, offers, and messages across channels in real time.

JO06.name: Monthly journey operations and optimization
JO06.scope: Each month, review journey and campaign reports, fix errors and bottlenecks, run content experiments, and tune frequency and quiet hours rules.
JO06.evidence: Monitor and optimize. Track performance and improve results over time

JO03.name: IP warmup plan execution
JO03.src: Get started with IP warmup plans
JO03.scope: Create the warmup campaigns, load the warmup plan, run each phase and watch delivery and reputation signals until sending volume reaches its target.
JO03.evidence: To avoid being marked as spam, you can progressively increase the volume sent using the IP warmup plan feature.

C06.name: Audiences that act on the data

CJ01.name: CJA data preparation in Experience Platform
CJ01.scope: Design the XDM schemas, create the datasets and set up ingestion for the channels CJA will report on, such as web, app, call center and point of sale data.
CJ01.evidence: Use Adobe Experience Data Model (XDM) to standardize customer experience data and define schemas

CJ02.name: Connections, data views and stitching
CJ02.scope: Create the connection with the right person ID for each dataset, turn on field-based or graph-based stitching in the connection where needed, and build data views with the client's components and settings.
CJ02.evidence: A connection lets you integrate datasets from Adobe Experience Platform into Workspace.

CJ03.name: Adobe Analytics upgrade to CJA
CJ03.src: Upgrade from Adobe Analytics to Customer Journey Analytics
CJ03.scope: Plan the upgrade path, implement Web SDK alongside the Analytics source connector for history, port reporting API use and exports, and migrate projects and components.
CJ03.evidence: a new implementation of the Experience Platform Web SDK, which is the preferred data collection method

CJ04.name: Workspace projects and dashboards
CJ04.scope: Build the starting Analysis Workspace projects and dashboards for each team's priority questions, with cross-channel journeys, KPIs and segments.
CJ04.evidence: analyze the data you have brought in using the power and flexibility of Analysis Workspace

CJ05.name: User onboarding and training
CJ05.scope: Plan role-based onboarding, train users on Analysis Workspace and on what differs from Adobe Analytics, and set up shared components and templates.
CJ05.evidence: give your users ample time (3 - 6 months) to become familiar with the key differences

CJ06.name: Monthly journey analysis and insights
CJ06.scope: Each month, run flow, fallout and attribution analysis on priority journeys, report findings to stakeholders and recommend next actions.
CJ06.evidence: Advanced analysis leverages features like Flow diagrams, Attribution, Fallout diagrams, and dimension breakdowns.

SI01.name: Cloud Manager program, pipelines and access
SI01.src: Experience League: AEM as a Cloud Service Onboarding Journey Introduction
SI01.scope: Assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager, set up Git access and the first deployment pipelines.
SI01.evidence: Cloud Manager - Set up programs and environments, access Git, and create pipelines to manage and deploy custom code.

SI02.name: Site build with components and templates
SI02.src: Experience League: Get started with AEM Sites - WKND tutorial
SI02.scope: Build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, with Core Components, editable templates, client-side libraries and the custom components the design needs.
SI02.evidence: The tutorial covers fundamental topics like project setup, Core Components, Editable Templates, Client-side libraries, and component development

SI04.name: Go-live checklist and cutover
SI04.scope: Work through Adobe's go-live checklist: a production pipeline with functional and UI tests, Dispatcher validation, CDN, SSL and DNS, performance and security tests on stage, notification profiles and traffic filter rules.
SI04.evidence: Run an end-to-end production pipeline with functional and UI testing to ensure an always current AEM product experience.

SI05.name: Author training on the Universal Editor
SI05.scope: Train authors to edit pages and content in the Universal Editor and hand over authoring guides for the site's components and templates.
SI05.evidence: It enables authors to perform what-you-see-is-what-you-get (WYSIWYG) editing of any headless or headful experience.

SI06.name: Monthly releases, monitoring and logs
SI06.scope: Each month, ship code through Cloud Manager pipelines, check the automatic AEM version updates, review logs and the Developer Console, and fix issues found after go-live.
SI06.evidence: monitor for issues and improve performance after the migration is complete

SI03.name: Content migration with Content Transfer Tool
SI03.src: Experience League: Overview to Content Transfer Tool
SI03.scope: For clients moving from AEM on-premise or Adobe Managed Services: extract and ingest content with the Content Transfer Tool in Cloud Acceleration Manager, then run differential top-ups before go-live.
SI03.evidence: migration of existing content from a source AEM instance (on-premise or AMS) to the target AEM Cloud Service instance

AS01.name: DAM onboarding, users and access
AS01.src: Experience League: Onboarding Agentic Capabilities Overview
AS01.scope: Add users to the Admin Console, create user groups and attach the AEM Assets product profiles, and confirm the Cloud Manager program and environments for the DAM.
AS01.evidence: Adds users to the Adobe Admin Console organization, creates user groups, and attaches product profiles to groups.

AS02.name: Folder structure, tags and metadata forms
AS02.src: Experience League: Onboarding Agentic Capabilities Overview
AS02.scope: Design the folder hierarchy under /content/dam, the controlled tag taxonomy and the custom metadata forms, so assets are findable and ready to reuse in every channel.
AS02.evidence: Designs and creates folder hierarchies under /content/dam and controlled tag taxonomies under /content/cq:tags

AS03.name: Asset and metadata migration
AS03.src: Experience League: Bulk import assets using Assets view
AS03.scope: Bulk import the existing library from cloud storage (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Dropbox or OneDrive) and load metadata for existing assets from CSV files.
AS03.evidence: import large numbers of assets directly from an external data source into AEM Assets in a single, streamlined operation

AS04.name: Processing profiles and renditions
AS04.src: Experience League: Add your digital assets to Adobe Experience Manager.
AS04.scope: Configure processing profiles on upload folders for the renditions, metadata and image processing each channel needs, plus any post-processing workflows.
AS04.evidence: Several asset processing profiles can be configured on the folder, into which assets are uploaded, to add specific metadata, renditions

AS06.name: Monthly DAM administration and reporting
AS06.src: Experience League: Reports about usage and sharing
AS06.scope: Each month, review asset reports on usage and sharing, tidy metadata and tags, update processing profiles and manage user access.
AS06.evidence: The reports provide useful information about your system’s usage, how users interact with assets, and which assets are shared.

AS05.name: Content Hub portal for approved assets
AS05.scope: Deploy Content Hub, set user, contributor and administrator roles, configure the portal, and set up the approval step that releases assets to it.
AS05.evidence: Only assets marked Approved on Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service become available for distribution on Content Hub

JB01.name: B2B schemas, XDM fields and events
JB01.scope: Generate the B2B namespaces and schemas with Adobe's utility, choose the managed and relational XDM fields for journeys and personalization, and select the Experience Platform events journeys listen to.
JB01.evidence: Run the Namespaces and Schemas generation utility in Postman and confirm namespaces and schemas are created.

JB02.name: Email domains and deliverability setup
JB02.scope: In the attached Marketo Engage instance, set up tracking CNAMEs, branding domains, DKIM, SPF, DMARC and MX records and IP allowlists, then email settings and communication limits in the B2B Edition.
JB02.evidence: configure the email tracking and deliverability in the attached Marketo Engage production instance

JB03.name: Buying groups and solution interests
JB03.scope: Define solution interests and role templates with sales, build account audiences, and run the buying group creation jobs that fill each buying group.
JB03.evidence: Before you create buying groups, you should know what you are selling and who you want to target.

JB04.name: First account journeys and email content
JB04.scope: Build the first account journeys for acquisition or cross-sell, with personalized email templates, visual fragments and journey nodes, then test and publish them.
JB04.evidence: Tailor your journeys for each buying group and buying group member using automated engagement across email, SMS, events, and more.

JB05.name: User roles, access and team enablement
JB05.scope: Create the product profile and user groups in the Admin Console, configure B2B user roles, add users, and walk marketers through Adobe's onboarding guidance.
JB05.evidence: configure Journey Optimizer B2B Edition and Marketo Engage access for your team and users.

JB06.name: Monthly buying group and journey reviews
JB06.scope: Each month, review the Intelligent Dashboard and journey results, refresh buying groups and audiences, and tune journeys and content.
JB06.evidence: The Intelligent Dashboard provides a comprehensive view of buying group and account metrics, helping you to monitor and strategize

EX01.name: Accelerator access, roles and sandboxes
EX01.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
EX01.scope: Add the Experiment accelerator resource to roles with View Experiments or Manage Experiment Metadata, assign the sandboxes, and add users.
EX01.evidence: Add the Experiment accelerator resource, then select View Experiments and/or Manage Experiment Metada from the drop-down menu.

EX02.name: Experiment program and hypothesis playbook
EX02.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator best practices
EX02.scope: Set up the client's testing playbook: hypothesis format, primary and secondary metrics, sample size and run time, segmentation rules and how learnings are recorded.
EX02.evidence: A strong hypothesis includes what you’re changing, what you expect to happen, and why.

EX03.name: Hypotheses and treatment details per test
EX03.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
EX03.scope: Add a hypothesis and confirm the treatment details and screenshots for each running experiment, which the accelerator needs before it generates insights and opportunities.
EX03.evidence: for Experiment insights to be generated, you need to confirm hypothesis and treatment details and statistical significance to be reached.

EX05.name: Training on insights and opportunities
EX05.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
EX05.scope: Train marketers and analysts to read experiment outcomes, insights and AI opportunities, including learning and conversion potential, and to share results.
EX05.evidence: The Opportunities panel displays AI-generated recommendations designed to enhance test performance and align with broader business objectives and KPIs.

EX06.name: Monthly experiment review and backlog
EX06.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
EX06.scope: Each month, review the experiments list and KPIs, pick the opportunities worth testing next, and keep the test backlog and learnings log current.
EX06.evidence: The KPI section provides key metrics, including the total number of experiments created and the number currently in progress

EX04.name: Primary metrics from CJA or Adobe Analytics
EX04.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
EX04.scope: Where CJA or Adobe Analytics is the reporting source, choose and import the primary metric for each experiment; changes stay in the accelerator.
EX04.evidence: Changing the primary metric applies to teams that use Customer Journey Analytics or Adobe Analytics as the reporting source

CA01.name: Content Analytics readiness and prerequisites
CA01.scope: Confirm Web SDK or Mobile SDK data collection, allow-list the featurization service's user agent and IP, set CJA and data collection permissions, and agree which pages and assets to analyze.
CA01.evidence: You have allow-listed the User Agent and IP address for the featurization service that is used in Content Analytics.

CA02.name: Guided configuration and Tags rollout
CA02.scope: Run the guided configuration (sandbox, connection, data views, web and mobile channels, experience capture, exclusion rules that keep personal data out), implement it and publish the Tags property.
CA02.evidence: Only when you manually publish the Tags property is your Content Analytics configuration effectively deployed and data collection started.

CA05.name: Content Analytics reporting and training
CA05.scope: Set up the Content Analytics Workspace template and core freeform reports with thumbnails and previews, and train analysts and content teams to read attribute insights.
CA05.evidence: A specific Workspace template is available, so you can immediately access a pre-populated Workspace project with relevant content insights.

CA06.name: Monthly content performance insights
CA06.scope: Each month, review which assets and attributes drive engagement and conversion, flag underused or overused assets, and feed the findings into the content plan.
CA06.evidence: These insights help you to see whether assets are underused or overused on your web and mobile properties.

CA03.name: Experience versioning on web pages
CA03.src: Experience League: Content Analytics Manual Configuration
CA03.scope: Where page experiences are captured, add the adobe.getContentExperienceVersion function to the analyzed pages so page changes are recorded as new experiences.
CA03.evidence: you should consider implementing versioning to ensure new experiences (changes to your web page) are properly collected

CA04.name: Paid media channel setup
CA04.src: Experience League: Content Analytics Paid Media Automatic Configuration
CA04.scope: Enable the paid media channel on the ad datasets from Experience Platform's ad network source connectors, then map tracking keys so ad content links to site conversions.
CA04.evidence: The correlation between your experience event data and paid media data requires customer-specific tracking-key mapping and reporting configuration.

CO01.name: Collaboration access and roles setup
CO01.src: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide
CO01.scope: Grant administrator access, create Permissions roles that include the View Profiles and View Segments permissions audience sourcing needs, add sandboxes, assign users and confirm each one can open Collaboration.
CO01.evidence: Your organization's access roles determine what users can see and do in Collaboration.

CO02.name: Account, branding and match key setup
CO02.src: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide
CO02.scope: Agree the match key strategy with the client, create the advertiser or publisher account, add the name, description, logo and contact email, and configure the match keys used to align audiences.
CO02.evidence: Define your account's role in Collaboration, provide branding assets, and configure match keys to align audiences across connections.

CO04.name: Collaborator connections and first projects
CO04.src: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide
CO04.scope: Find publishers in the Connect workspace or send private invitations, agree connection settings such as use cases and credit consumption, confirm the connection and set up the first project with Discover, Activate and Measure.
CO04.evidence: involves sending or receiving invitations, reviewing and submitting connection settings (such as use cases and credit consumption)

CO05.name: Overlap and measurement reporting enablement
CO05.scope: Train the client team to read audience overlap insights, pick audiences to activate, add campaign IDs and create campaign summary and attribution reports in the Measure workspace.
CO05.evidence: Get insight into overlap percentages and the number of overlapping identities between your audiences and those of your collaborators.

CO06.name: Monthly collaboration operations
CO06.src: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide
CO06.scope: Each month, add or retire audiences, tune refresh schedules to manage credit use, set up projects for new campaigns and run overlap and measurement reports with collaborators.
CO06.evidence: You can add or remove audiences and update the refresh schedule directly in Collaboration.

CO03.name: Audience sourcing from cloud data sources
CO03.src: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration quick start guide
CO03.scope: For audiences kept outside Experience Platform, prepare files to Adobe's audience specification with SHA256-hashed identifiers and the required metadata, then set up the Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage or Snowflake data connection.
CO03.evidence: Cloud-based audience files must follow the required schema outlined in the Audience Specification PDF.

MM01.name: Access, roles and sandbox setup
MM01.src: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics administration
MM01.scope: Create the Permissions role with the Marketing Campaign Analytics resource and its harmonized data, model and plan permissions, add the sandboxes and dataset and schema permissions, and assign users.
MM01.evidence: For Marketing Campaign Analytics to function properly, you must set the correct permissions.

MM02.name: Marketing data ingestion and schemas
MM02.src: Experience League: Ingest data overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
MM02.scope: Model schemas on the XDM ExperienceEvent or Summary Metrics classes, then ingest channel spend and effort, conversions and internal and external factors with consistent dates, granularity and channel fields, and validate the loads.
MM02.evidence: Date and granularity are mandatory fields in the underlying schema for all aggregate data ingested as datasets

MM03.name: Harmonized data, touchpoints and conversions
MM03.src: Experience League: Harmonize datasets overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
MM03.scope: Define harmonized fields, write dataset rules for each aggregate, event and factor dataset, define marketing touchpoints and conversions, then sync and check the harmonized data.
MM03.evidence: Set up dataset rules to map fields from your aggregate (factor or summary) or experience event datasets to harmonized fields.

MM04.name: Model build, training and validation
MM04.src: Experience League: Models overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
MM04.scope: Configure models with the conversion, touchpoints, lookback and training windows, factors and priors, turn on multi-touch attribution or full funnel modeling where agreed, and retrain until the fit suits the business.
MM04.evidence: Retraining and rescoring are an iterative process as new findings and information emerge and adjustments are needed

MM05.name: Budget plans and team enablement
MM05.src: Experience League: Plans overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
MM05.scope: Build the first budget plans with flight dates and channel constraints, compare scenarios, and train marketing and finance users to read model and plan insights.
MM05.evidence: Plans in Marketing Campaign Analytics allow you to allocate budgets by business unit and channel.

MM06.name: Monthly data refresh, rescoring and plans
MM06.src: Experience League: Models overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
MM06.scope: Each month, load new spend, conversion and factor data, rescore or retrain models, rebuild plans on the rescored models and report ROI and budget shifts to stakeholders.
MM06.evidence: data may be added to the model which requires you to rescore the model manually.

GS01.name: Provisioning, roles and Brands permissions
GS01.src: Experience League: Get started with GenStudio for Performance Marketing
GS01.scope: Assign GenStudio licenses in the Admin Console to system managers, editors and collaborators, and create the user group and Admin Console project that Brands permissions need.
GS01.evidence: System administrators must complete additional set-up tasks before collaborators can edit or create Brands.

GS02.name: Brand, product and persona guidelines
GS02.src: Experience League: Get started with GenStudio for Performance Marketing
GS02.scope: Gather and tidy the client's brand, product and persona documents, upload or enter them with channel guidelines, logos, colors and tone of voice, then test generated output and publish.
GS02.evidence: Content editors and collaborators cannot begin their work until the foundational elements of your organization's brand identity are established.

GS03.name: Channel templates and approved assets
GS03.src: Experience League: Work with templates (GenStudio for Performance Marketing)
GS03.scope: Design and code responsive HTML templates for email, Meta, LinkedIn and display, add Handlebars content placeholders, upload and test them, and load the approved assets editors will use into Content.
GS03.evidence: Adapt your HTML template using the Handlebars templating language.

GS04.name: Paid media connections and activation setup
GS04.src: Experience League: GenStudio for Performance Marketing Activate
GS04.scope: Connect the client's Meta, LinkedIn and Campaign Manager 360 accounts with the right ad account permissions, confirm historical data reaches Insights, and test activation into existing campaigns and ad sets.
GS04.evidence: A GenStudio system manager or editor must connect the ad account for each paid ad channel before you can activate

GS05.name: Editor training and first campaign launch
GS05.src: Experience League: GenStudio for Performance Marketing user roles and permissions
GS05.scope: Train editors and approvers on prompting, creating experiences, review and approval and activation, while running the first campaign end to end with the client team.
GS05.evidence: the quality and success of generated content partially depend on the quality of the brand guidelines your organization has uploaded

GS06.name: Monthly content refresh from Insights
GS06.src: Experience League: GenStudio for Performance Marketing Insights
GS06.scope: Each month, review Insights by campaign, media and attribute, generate and approve variants for weak ads, refresh hero content and update guidelines and templates as the brand changes.
GS06.evidence: Find content that is not performing well and use the integrated generative AI to create variations immediately

C01.name: Connect Brand Visibility and CJA measurement
C01.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility and CJA integration

BVCJ2.name: Rank AI sources by the value they send
BVCJ2.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility and CJA integration
BVCJ2.scope: Send CJA performance data into Brand Visibility, rank the AI sources by the visitors and conversions they send, and agree which sources the AI visibility work targets first.
BVCJ2.evidence: Send Customer Journey Analytics performance data into Brand Visibility

C03.name: AEM optimization publishing workflow
C03.src: Adobe news: Introducing Adobe Brand Visibility

SO1.name: Sites Optimizer setup
SO1.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer opportunity types

C02.name: Commerce product-content enrichment pilot
C02.src: Experience League: Enrich Product Detail Pages

C07.name: CDN readiness for stores not on Fastly
C07.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility, Optimize at Edge

RC01.name: Real-Time CDP audience analysis in CJA
RC01.scope: Configure audience analysis by choosing the sandbox, merge policy, connection and data views (Adobe then creates the lookup dataset, audience dimensions and data view settings), and extend Adobe's Audience overview template with the client's KPIs.
RC01.evidence: Audience analysis allows you to ingest audience membership data from Experience Platform Profile datasets into a Customer Journey Analytics connection.

RC02.name: Identity and audience count alignment
RC02.src: Consistency of metrics and audience membership
RC02.scope: Align the CJA person ID and stitching method with the Real-Time CDP identity graph, agree which datasets and retention windows each app uses, and document expected audience count differences for stakeholders.
RC02.evidence: Real-time CDP and Customer Journey Analytics do not share the same definition of a person today.

RC03.name: Journey audiences from CJA for activation
RC03.src: Experience League: How Experience Platform and its applications work together
RC03.scope: Define up to five audiences from cross-channel journey behavior in CJA, publish them to Experience Platform, and set up their activation in Real-Time CDP with the customer.
RC03.evidence: Audiences you define in Customer Journey Analytics can be published to Adobe Experience Platform

XD01.name: Experience Platform audience sourcing
XD01.src: Experience League: Source and manage audiences (Collaboration)
XD01.scope: Create the Experience Platform data connection, pick the sandbox, set marketing actions and consent rules, map identities and profile attributes to match keys with hashing, schedule refreshes and select the audiences.
XD01.evidence: Any settings that you configure for an Experience Platform data connection are applied to all audiences sourced from that connection.

XD02.name: Experience Platform destination setup
XD02.src: Experience League: Configure Adobe Experience Platform as a destination (Collaboration)
XD02.scope: Create the Experience Platform destination before collaborators activate, map match keys to hashed identity namespaces, set linked keys and expiration, verify audiences in Audience Portal and apply data usage labels.
XD02.evidence: You must configure Experience Platform as a destination before your collaborator activates an audience.

XD03.name: Conversion data for Collaboration measurement
XD03.src: Experience League: Add and manage measurement data (Collaboration)
XD03.scope: Source the conversion event dataset from Experience Platform, map identities to match keys, enrich events with Real-Time Customer Profile attributes, and set the duplication key and conditions for attribution reports.
XD03.evidence: You can also choose to enrich your event dataset with attributes from Real-Time Customer Profile by mapping join keys

XD04.name: Lookalike audiences from MMM top segments
XD04.src: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics use cases
XD04.scope: Read the touchpoint scores to find the highest-value consumer segments, rebuild them as base audiences in Experience Platform on the default merge policy, then create lookalike audiences and activate them.
XD04.evidence: Create and activate lookalikes to top consumer segments using Real-Time Customer Data Platform.

XD05.name: Real-Time CDP conversion data for MMM
XD05.src: Experience League: Harmonize datasets overview (Marketing Campaign Analytics)
XD05.scope: Reuse the conversion and event datasets already ingested for Real-Time CDP, such as CRM, commerce and web data, as Mix Modeler event inputs, checking identities on each event dataset.
XD05.evidence: Ensure you have set up identities properly for each of the event datasets.

XD06.name: Content engagement audiences for activation
XD06.src: Adobe: Adobe Content Analytics product page
XD06.scope: Build segments on Content Analytics asset and experience attributes in Workspace, publish them as audiences to Real-Time Customer Profile, and set up their activation in Real-Time CDP.
XD06.evidence: Create activation-ready audiences from content engagement and immediately share them across other Adobe products.

XD07.name: Touchpoint scores in CJA connections
XD07.src: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics use cases
XD07.scope: Add the Mix Modeler aggregate and event score datasets to a CJA connection, set the person ID for event scores, and build data view metrics and dimensions for scores, channels and touchpoints.
XD07.evidence: Export incremental touchpoint scores into Customer Journey Analytics or external BI tools.

XD08.name: Incrementality dashboards in Workspace
XD08.src: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics use cases
XD08.scope: Build Workspace projects that break incremental and influenced scores down by segment, campaign and journey, next to CJA conversion metrics.
XD08.evidence: Perform granular analysis and build advanced dashboards using touchpoint scores.

XD09.name: CJA event data reuse in Mix Modeler
XD09.src: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics use cases
XD09.scope: Map the web and app event datasets already behind CJA into Mix Modeler dataset rules as touchpoints and conversions, and align conversion definitions so both apps report matching totals.
XD09.evidence: Apply existing investments in Adobe Analytics or Customer Journey Analytics to fast-track deployment.

XD10.name: Shared paid media data for MMM and CA
XD10.src: Adobe: Marketing Campaign Analytics paid media analysis
XD10.scope: Use one set of Experience Platform paid media connectors for both apps by mapping the paid media summary datasets into Mix Modeler dataset rules and aligning channel and campaign naming with Content Analytics.
XD10.evidence: Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics connects to paid media data via Adobe Experience Platform paid media connectors and ETL partners

XD11.name: Monthly channel and creative review
XD11.src: Adobe: Marketing Campaign Analytics (formerly Mix Modeler) product page
XD11.scope: Each month, read Mix Modeler channel and campaign incrementality next to Content Analytics attribute performance, and recommend budget shifts and creative changes for paid media.
XD11.evidence: Align channel- and campaign-level insight from Marketing Campaign Analytics with content and attribute-level insight

XD12.name: Content Analytics in existing data views
XD12.src: Experience League: Content Analytics guided configuration
XD12.scope: Review what adding Content Analytics changes in the client's existing CJA data views, check person IDs and stitching so content events join existing journeys, and reconcile its components with existing segments and metrics.
XD12.evidence: a Selected data views dialog that informs you about implications of including Content Analytics for the selected data views

XD13.name: Content journey and conversion analysis
XD13.scope: Extend the Content Analytics Workspace template with flow, fallout and attribution panels that tie assets, experiences and attributes to conversions and journey stages.
XD13.evidence: when combined with all other data available in Experience Platform, you can gain additional insights on your content journeys

XD14.name: Tracking keys on GenStudio-activated ads
XD14.src: Experience League: Activate a Meta ad (GenStudio for Performance Marketing)
XD14.scope: Confirm the ad accounts GenStudio activates into are connected as Experience Platform paid media sources for Content Analytics, then agree a tracking ID and URL parameter convention and apply it at activation.
XD14.evidence: Destination URL, URL Parameters, Tracking ID (used as the Meta ad name)

XD15.name: Monthly attribute insights to new variants
XD15.scope: Each month, pull the strongest and weakest creative attributes from Content Analytics, turn them into GenStudio prompts and briefs, generate and approve variants, and retire weak ads.
XD15.evidence: teams can improve creative performance and conversions by understanding what's working down to the attribute level

XC01.name: Connect Sites to the DAM with OpenAPI
XC01.src: Experience League: Integrate remote AEM Assets with AEM Sites
XC01.scope: Set the asset delivery repository and IMS client variables in Cloud Manager, configure the Image v3 component and HTTPS, and confirm authors can pick remote assets.
XC01.evidence: Set up the following environment variables for AEM as a Cloud Service

XC02.name: Image modifiers and smart crops for pages
XC02.src: Experience League: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI capabilities
XC02.scope: Set up the image modifiers and smart crops each page component uses, so every placement gets the right size and format from the DAM.
XC02.evidence: on-the-fly image transformation using URL parameters known as image modifiers

XC03.name: AEM Assets repository in Journey Optimizer
XC03.src: Experience League: Use Assets in Journey Optimizer
XC03.scope: Add marketers to the Assets Cloud Services product profiles, select the Assets as a Cloud Service repository in Journey Optimizer, and set up campaign asset folders.
XC03.evidence: Before using Adobe Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service, you must add users to Assets Cloud Services.

XC04.name: Dynamic Media renditions in journey content
XC04.src: Experience League: Combine solutions and apps to manage your content
XC04.scope: For clients with Dynamic Media, set up the approved renditions and smart crops marketers pick in Content Advisor, so journey content always uses the latest version.
XC04.evidence: Dynamic media allowing you to seamlessly select and use approved dynamic media renditions within Journey Optimizer

XC05.name: Content Fragments for Journey Optimizer
XC05.scope: Allow the Content Fragment API in the Dispatcher, create the ajo-enabled tag for each sandbox, model channel-ready fragments, and publish them for campaigns and journeys.
XC05.evidence: Content Fragments must be tagged with the Journey Optimizer-specific tag (ajo-enabled:{OrgId}/{SandboxName}).

XC06.name: Personalized fragments and variations
XC06.scope: Add placeholders to fragment text and map them to profile or contextual attributes in Journey Optimizer, and set up fragment variations for audiences or channels.
XC06.evidence: To enable real-time personalization, all placeholders used within a Content fragment must be explicitly declared by the user as parameters

XC07.name: AJO references and previews in AEM
XC07.src: Experience League: Using the Content Fragments AJO External References Extension
XC07.scope: Enable the AJO External References extension so authors see and preview the campaigns, journeys and templates that use a fragment before they change it.
XC07.evidence: fetching references to Content Fragment from all organizations and sandboxes associated with predefined tags

XC08.name: Content experiments in Journey Optimizer
XC08.src: Experience League: Get started with content experiment
XC08.scope: Set up content experiments in campaigns and journeys, with the identity namespace for random assignment, the treatments and the success metrics, so they flow into the accelerator.
XC08.evidence: as part of configuring every campaign with a content experiment, you must choose an identity namespace

XC09.name: Turn opportunities into AJO tests
XC09.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
XC09.scope: Agree how an accepted opportunity becomes a new treatment: open it in the campaign's Content Experimentation panel, build and check the variant, and relaunch.
XC09.evidence: this action will open the Content Experimentation Panel within that campaign

XC10.name: Connect AEM Sites to Commerce with CIF
XC10.src: Experience League: Getting started with AEM Commerce as a Cloud Service
XC10.scope: Once Adobe provisions the CIF add-on, set the COMMERCE_ENDPOINT variable for each environment in Cloud Manager and the CIF configuration for store view and catalog root.
XC10.evidence: you must provide the GraphQL endpoint URL by way of a Cloud Manager environment variable. The variable name is COMMERCE_ENDPOINT.

XC11.name: Product-enriched content experiences
XC11.scope: Build the commerce-specific content (product teasers, category and campaign content, Content Fragments) that authors assemble from products they search and browse in AEM.
XC11.evidence: a seamless integration of your product data into AEM (Search, browse, and find products within the AEM UI)

XC13.name: Set up AEM Assets for Commerce metadata
XC13.src: Experience League: Configure the AEM Assets Project
XC13.scope: Enable the Commerce integration in Cloud Manager (or install the assets-commerce package on older releases), activate Dynamic Media with OpenAPI, and set the approval metadata schema.
XC13.evidence: enable the integration in Cloud Manager by setting an environment variable and activating Dynamic Media with OpenAPI capabilities

XC14.name: Connect Commerce and set SKU matching
XC14.scope: Set IMS permissions and the AEM Assets Integration settings in the Commerce Admin, choose Match by product SKU, set the Visualization Owner and start the first sync.
XC14.evidence: matches the SKU in the asset metadata with the Commerce product SKU

XC15.name: Migrate Commerce media to AEM Assets
XC15.src: Experience League: Migrate media files to AEM
XC15.scope: Move existing product and category media from Commerce into AEM Assets, tag SKUs, roles and positions, and approve, keeping Commerce as Visualization Owner until the sync completes.
XC15.evidence: provide built-in features to streamline media file migration from Commerce to the AEM Assets digital asset management system

XC16.name: Custom asset matching with App Builder
XC16.scope: Where SKU matching is not enough, build custom matching logic in Adobe Developer App Builder that maps assets to products.
XC16.evidence: Implementing custom matching requires developing custom code in Adobe Developer App Builder to define how assets are matched with products.

XC17.name: Connect AEM Assets to AJO B2B Edition
XC17.src: Experience League: Configure Experience Manager Asset Repositories
XC17.scope: Generate service credentials in the AEM Headless Developer Console, add each repository and certificate in the B2B Edition, add users to the Assets product profiles, and plan the yearly certificate renewal.
XC17.evidence: Generate service credentials for the desired environment on the AEM Headless Developer Console

XC18.name: Re-link email images to AEM Assets
XC18.scope: For email templates imported with images, upload those images to AEM Assets and change the image links in the email design space, since imports land in the Marketo Engage asset store.
XC18.evidence: upload them separately in that app interface and change the image links in the email design space
